questions.question: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
answer_steps: A magnesium ribbon gets a layer of magnesium oxide on standing in air.
Rubbing it with sandpaper removes this layer, so the pure metal can burn properly.

questions.question:
Write the balanced equation for the following chemical reactions.

(i) Hydrogen + Chlorine → Hydrogen chloride

(ii) Barium chloride + Aluminium sulphate → Barium sulphate + Aluminium chloride

(iii) Sodium + Water → Sodium hydroxide + Hydrogen
answer_steps: (i) $\mathrm{H_{2} + Cl_{2} \rightarrow 2HCl}$
(ii) $\mathrm{3BaCl_{2} + Al_{2}(SO_{4})_{3} \rightarrow 3BaSO_{4} + 2AlCl_{3}}$
(iii) $\mathrm{2Na + 2H_{2}O \rightarrow 2NaOH + H_{2}}$

questions.question:
Write a balanced chemical equation with state symbols for the following reactions.

(i) Solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate in water react to give insoluble barium sulphate and the solution of sodium chloride.

(ii) Sodium hydroxide solution (in water) reacts with hydrochloric acid solution (in water) to produce sodium chloride solution and water.
answer_steps: (i) $\mathrm{BaCl_{2}(aq) + Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_{2}O(l)}$

questions.question:
A solution of a substance 'X' is used for whitewashing.

(i) Name the substance 'X' and write its formula.

(ii) Write the reaction of the substance 'X' named in (i) above with water.
answer_steps: (i) X is calcium oxide (quicklime), $\mathrm{CaO}$.
(ii) $\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$ (slaked lime forms and heat is given out).

questions.question: Why is the amount of gas collected in one of the test tubes in Activity 1.7 double of the amount collected in the other? Name this gas.
answer_steps: Water is broken down by electricity: $\mathrm{2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2H_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)}$
Each water molecule gives two hydrogen atoms for one oxygen atom, so the volume of hydrogen is double that of oxygen. The gas is hydrogen.

questions.question: Why does the colour of copper sulphate solution change when an iron nail is dipped in it?
answer_steps: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper: $\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$
Blue copper sulphate is used up and pale green iron sulphate forms, so the colour changes.

questions.question: Give an example of a double displacement reaction other than the one given in Activity 1.10.
answer_steps: Lead nitrate and potassium iodide exchange ions:
$\mathrm{Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_{2}(s) + 2KNO_{3}(aq)}$ (a yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms).

questions.question:
Identify the substances that are oxidised and the substances that are reduced in the following reactions.

(i) $\mathrm{4Na(s) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2Na_{2}O(s)}$

(ii) $\mathrm{CuO(s) + H_{2}(g) \rightarrow Cu(s) + H_{2}O(l)}$
answer_steps: (i) Sodium gains oxygen, so sodium is oxidised and oxygen is reduced.
(ii) Copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced; hydrogen gains oxygen, so it is oxidised.

questions.question:
Which of the statements about the reaction below are incorrect?

$\mathrm{2PbO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow 2Pb(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$

(a) Lead is getting reduced.
(b) Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised.
(c) Carbon is getting oxidised.
(d) Lead oxide is getting reduced.
questions.explanation: Lead oxide (not lead) is reduced, and carbon dioxide is a product, not something being oxidised. So (a) and (b) are incorrect; (c) and (d) are correct.
option_feedback: Correct!
(c) is correct: carbon gains oxygen and is oxidised.
(c) is a correct statement.
(c) and (d) are correct statements.

questions.question:
$\mathrm{Fe_{2}O_{3} + 2Al \rightarrow Al_{2}O_{3} + 2Fe}$

The above reaction is an example of a
questions.explanation: Aluminium, an element, displaces iron from its oxide.
option_feedback: There are two products, not one.
Aluminium is an element, not a compound.
Two substances react; nothing breaks up on its own.
Correct!

questions.question: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron filings?
options: Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced.
Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced.
Iron salt and water are produced.
questions.explanation: Iron displaces hydrogen from the acid: $\mathrm{Fe + 2HCl \rightarrow FeCl_{2} + H_{2}}$
option_feedback: Correct!
Iron displaces hydrogen, not chlorine.
Iron is more reactive than hydrogen.
Water forms when an acid reacts with a base, not a metal.

questions.question: What is a balanced chemical equation? Why should chemical equations be balanced?
answer_steps: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on the reactant and product sides.
Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a reaction (law of conservation of mass), so the equation must be balanced.

questions.question:
Translate the following statements into chemical equations and then balance them.

(a) Hydrogen gas combines with nitrogen to form ammonia.

(b) Hydrogen sulphide gas burns in air to give water and sulphur dioxide.

(c) Barium chloride reacts with aluminium sulphate to give aluminium chloride and a precipitate of barium sulphate.

(d) Potassium metal reacts with water to give potassium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
answer_steps: (a) $\mathrm{3H_{2}(g) + N_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2NH_{3}(g)}$
(b) $\mathrm{2H_{2}S(g) + 3O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2H_{2}O(l) + 2SO_{2}(g)}$
(c) $\mathrm{3BaCl_{2}(aq) + Al_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}(aq) \rightarrow 2AlCl_{3}(aq) + 3BaSO_{4}(s)}$
(d) $\mathrm{2K(s) + 2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2KOH(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$

questions.question:
Balance the following chemical equations.

(a) $\mathrm{HNO_{3} + Ca(OH)_{2} \rightarrow Ca(NO_{3})_{2} + H_{2}O}$

(b) $\mathrm{NaOH + H_{2}SO_{4} \rightarrow Na_{2}SO_{4} + H_{2}O}$

(c) $\mathrm{NaCl + AgNO_{3} \rightarrow AgCl + NaNO_{3}}$

(d) $\mathrm{BaCl_{2} + H_{2}SO_{4} \rightarrow BaSO_{4} + HCl}$
answer_steps: (a) $\mathrm{2HNO_{3} + Ca(OH)_{2} \rightarrow Ca(NO_{3})_{2} + 2H_{2}O}$
(b) $\mathrm{2NaOH + H_{2}SO_{4} \rightarrow Na_{2}SO_{4} + 2H_{2}O}$
(c) $\mathrm{NaCl + AgNO_{3} \rightarrow AgCl + NaNO_{3}}$ (already balanced)
(d) $\mathrm{BaCl_{2} + H_{2}SO_{4} \rightarrow BaSO_{4} + 2HCl}$

questions.question:
Write the balanced chemical equations for the following reactions.

(a) Calcium hydroxide + Carbon dioxide → Calcium carbonate + Water

(b) Zinc + Silver nitrate → Zinc nitrate + Silver

(c) Aluminium + Copper chloride → Aluminium chloride + Copper

(d) Barium chloride + Potassium sulphate → Barium sulphate + Potassium chloride
answer_steps: (a) $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_{2} + CO_{2} \rightarrow CaCO_{3} + H_{2}O}$
(b) $\mathrm{Zn + 2AgNO_{3} \rightarrow Zn(NO_{3})_{2} + 2Ag}$
(c) $\mathrm{2Al + 3CuCl_{2} \rightarrow 2AlCl_{3} + 3Cu}$
(d) $\mathrm{BaCl_{2} + K_{2}SO_{4} \rightarrow BaSO_{4} + 2KCl}$

questions.question:
Write the balanced chemical equation for the following and identify the type of reaction in each case.

(a) Potassium bromide(aq) + Barium iodide(aq) → Potassium iodide(aq) + Barium bromide(s)

(b) Zinc carbonate(s) → Zinc oxide(s) + Carbon dioxide(g)

(c) Hydrogen(g) + Chlorine(g) → Hydrogen chloride(g)

(d) Magnesium(s) + Hydrochloric acid(aq) → Magnesium chloride(aq) + Hydrogen(g)
answer_steps: (a) $\mathrm{2KBr(aq) + BaI_{2}(aq) \rightarrow 2KI(aq) + BaBr_{2}(s)}$: double displacement (and precipitation)
(b) $\mathrm{ZnCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} ZnO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$: decomposition
(c) $\mathrm{H_{2}(g) + Cl_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2HCl(g)}$: combination
(d) $\mathrm{Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) \rightarrow MgCl_{2}(aq) + H_{2}(g)}$: displacement

questions.question: What does one mean by exothermic and endothermic reactions? Give examples.
answer_steps: Exothermic reactions give out heat, for example burning natural gas: $\mathrm{CH_{4}(g) + 2O_{2}(g) \rightarrow CO_{2}(g) + 2H_{2}O(g)}$
Endothermic reactions absorb energy, for example the decomposition of calcium carbonate: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$
Respiration is exothermic; photosynthesis and the decomposition of silver chloride in sunlight absorb energy.

questions.question: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Explain.
answer_steps: In respiration, glucose combines with oxygen in our cells: $\mathrm{C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}(aq) + 6O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 6CO_{2}(g) + 6H_{2}O(l)}$
Energy is released in this reaction, so it is exothermic.

questions.question: Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
answer_steps: In a combination reaction, two or more substances form one product; in a decomposition reaction, one substance breaks into two or more.
Combination: $\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$
Decomposition: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: Write one equation each for decomposition reactions where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light or electricity.
answer_steps: Heat: $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$
Light: $\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \rightarrow 2Ag(s) + Cl_{2}(g)}$
Electricity: $\mathrm{2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2H_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: What is the difference between displacement and double displacement reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
answer_steps: In a displacement reaction a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound: $\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$
In a double displacement reaction two compounds exchange ions: $\mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$
So displacement involves an element and a compound; double displacement involves two compounds.

questions.question: In the refining of silver, the recovery of silver from silver nitrate solution involved displacement by copper metal. Write down the reaction involved.
answer_steps: $\mathrm{Cu(s) + 2AgNO_{3}(aq) \rightarrow Cu(NO_{3})_{2}(aq) + 2Ag(s)}$
Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver.

questions.question: What do you mean by a precipitation reaction? Explain by giving examples.
answer_steps: A reaction in which an insoluble substance (precipitate) forms is a precipitation reaction.
Example: $\mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$ (white precipitate)
Example: $\mathrm{Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_{2}(s) + 2KNO_{3}(aq)}$ (yellow precipitate)

questions.question:
Explain the following in terms of gain or loss of oxygen with two examples each.

(a) Oxidation

(b) Reduction
answer_steps: (a) Oxidation is the gain of oxygen: $\mathrm{2Cu + O_{2} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2CuO}$ (copper is oxidised); $\mathrm{C(s) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow CO_{2}(g)}$ (carbon is oxidised).
(b) Reduction is the loss of oxygen: $\mathrm{CuO + H_{2} \xrightarrow{\Delta} Cu + H_{2}O}$ (copper oxide is reduced); $\mathrm{ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO}$ (zinc oxide is reduced).
In each pair, one substance is oxidised while the other is reduced.
marking_scheme: 1 mark: naming what is oxidised and reduced

questions.question: A shiny brown coloured element 'X' on heating in air becomes black in colour. Name the element 'X' and the black coloured compound formed.
answer_steps: X is copper; the black compound is copper(II) oxide, $\mathrm{CuO}$.
$\mathrm{2Cu + O_{2} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2CuO}$

questions.question: Why do we apply paint on iron articles?
answer_steps: Iron rusts when it is exposed to moist air.
Paint keeps air and moisture away from the iron, so it prevents rusting (corrosion).

questions.question: Oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen. Why?
answer_steps: Oxygen in air oxidises oils and fats, making the food rancid (bad smell and taste).
Nitrogen is unreactive and keeps oxygen away, so it prevents rancidity.

questions.question:
Explain the following terms with one example each.

(a) Corrosion

(b) Rancidity
answer_steps: (a) Corrosion: a metal is slowly eaten away by moisture, air or acids. Example: iron gets a reddish-brown coating of rust; silver turns black.
(b) Rancidity: fats and oils in food get oxidised, changing their smell and taste. Example: chips or butter kept open for a long time.
Painting prevents corrosion; nitrogen or antioxidants prevent rancidity.

questions.question:
Which of the following equations represent redox reactions and what are the values for 'p' and 'q' in these equations?

Equation 1: $\mathrm{Fe_{2}O_{3}(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow Al_{2}O_{3}(s) + p\,Fe(l)}$ + heat

Equation 2: $\mathrm{2C_{4}H_{10}(g) + 13O_{2}(g) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 8CO_{2}(g) + q\,H_{2}O(g)}$
options: Only equation 1 is a redox reaction, p = 1 and q = 3
Both equations 1 and 2 are redox reactions, p = 2 and q = 4
Only equation 2 is a redox reaction, p = 2 and q = 10
Both equations 1 and 2 are redox reactions, p = 2 and q = 10
questions.explanation: Balancing gives p = 2 (2 Fe atoms) and q = 10 (20 H atoms). In both, one substance gains oxygen while another loses it or burns, so both are redox reactions.
option_feedback: Count the atoms again: 2 Fe and 20 H.
There are 20 hydrogen atoms in $\mathrm{2C_{4}H_{10}}$.
Equation 1 is also redox: Al is oxidised, Fe₂O₃ is reduced.
Correct!

questions.question: In the reaction of aqueous solution of barium chloride with aqueous solution of sodium sulphate, the aqueous solution formed will be:
questions.explanation: Barium sulphate is the insoluble precipitate; sodium chloride stays dissolved: $\mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$
option_feedback: It is used up in the reaction.
It is the insoluble precipitate.
It is used up in the reaction.
Correct!

questions.question:
Amrita set up an electrolysis apparatus with distilled water, expecting two gases to be evolved at the anode and the cathode. She realised that the bulb in the circuit did not glow when she used distilled water. She then added a substance to the distilled water so that electrolysis could take place.

A. Which gas was she expecting to be formed at the anode and which one at the cathode?

B. Why did the bulb not glow when Amrita passed electricity through distilled water?

C. Which substance was added by Amrita to distilled water to get the expected result?
answer_steps: A. Oxygen at the anode and hydrogen at the cathode.
B. Distilled water is a poor conductor of electricity: it has almost no ions.
C. A few drops of dilute sulphuric acid (or some sodium chloride, any strong electrolyte).

questions.question:
Identify the type of reaction:

A. $\mathrm{ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO}$

B. $\mathrm{ZnCO_{3} \xrightarrow{\Delta} ZnO + CO_{2}}$

C. $\mathrm{2Mg + O_{2} \rightarrow 2MgO}$ + heat
answer_steps: A. Redox reaction (zinc oxide is reduced, carbon is oxidised).
B. Decomposition reaction; it is endothermic.
C. Combination reaction; it is exothermic.

questions.question:
Silver chloride is kept in a china dish in sunlight.

(a) Identify the type of chemical reaction and define it.

(b) Write the change in colour of the salt placed in the china dish.

(c) Write the balanced chemical equation of the reaction.
answer_steps: (a) Decomposition reaction (by light): a single substance breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
(b) White silver chloride turns grey.
(c) $\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \rightarrow 2Ag(s) + Cl_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: What is a combination reaction? Explain with two examples.
answer_steps: In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product.
Example: $\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$
Example: $\mathrm{C(s) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow CO_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: Which state symbol shows a solution in water?
questions.explanation: (aq) stands for aqueous: dissolved in water.
option_feedback: (g) means a gas.
Correct!
(l) means a liquid.
(s) means a solid.

questions.question: When quicklime reacts with water, the reaction is:
questions.explanation: Calcium oxide and water combine into one product and give out a lot of heat.
option_feedback: Correct!
Two substances combine, and heat is given out.
Nothing is displaced.
The mixture gets hot: heat is given out.

questions.question: On heating, green ferrous sulphate crystals give a smell of burning sulphur. The residue is:
questions.explanation: Ferrous sulphate decomposes into ferric oxide (brown), sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide.
option_feedback: The residue is brown.
There is no copper here.
It decomposes; it does not stay the same.
Correct!

questions.question: In the electrolysis of water, the ratio of the volumes of hydrogen and oxygen collected is:
questions.explanation: Water has two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen atom.
option_feedback: Water has twice as many hydrogen atoms as oxygen atoms.
That is the ratio by mass, not by volume.
Correct!
Hydrogen is the larger volume.

questions.question: Silver bromide is used in black and white photography because it:
questions.explanation: Light decomposes silver bromide into silver and bromine.
option_feedback: Photography uses its reaction to light.
Correct!
Light breaks it down; it does not combine.
It is insoluble.

questions.question: A yellow precipitate forms when lead nitrate solution is mixed with:
questions.explanation: Lead iodide, the yellow precipitate, forms by double displacement.
option_feedback: Correct!
Lead chloride is white, not yellow.
No yellow precipitate forms.
Water only dilutes it.

questions.question: Which of these is an oxidation?
options: Copper oxide turning into copper with hydrogen
Copper turning into copper oxide on heating
questions.explanation: Copper gains oxygen when it forms copper oxide.
option_feedback: That is reduction of copper oxide.
That is a physical change.
That is a physical change.

questions.question: Which metal can displace copper from copper sulphate solution?
questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper; silver, gold and platinum are less reactive.
option_feedback: Gold is less reactive than copper.
Platinum is less reactive than copper.
Correct!
Silver is less reactive than copper.

questions.question: To balance $\mathrm{Na + H_{2}O \rightarrow NaOH + H_{2}}$, the coefficients are:
questions.explanation: Balanced: $\mathrm{2Na + 2H_{2}O \rightarrow 2NaOH + H_{2}}$
option_feedback: Check the sodium atoms.
Correct!
That leaves 2 H on the left and 3 H on the right.
Check the oxygen and hydrogen atoms.

questions.question: The black coating on silver articles is an example of:
questions.explanation: Silver reacts slowly with sulphur compounds in air and gets a black coating: corrosion.
option_feedback: Silver combines with sulphur; it does not break up.
Correct!
Rancidity is about oils and fats in food.
No precipitate forms from a solution.

questions.question: Balance the equation: $\mathrm{Al + O_{2} \rightarrow Al_{2}O_{3}}$
answer_steps: $\mathrm{4Al + 3O_{2} \rightarrow 2Al_{2}O_{3}}$
Check: Al 4 = 4, O 6 = 6.

questions.question: Why does a lead nitrate crystal give off brown fumes on heating? Write the equation.
answer_steps: Lead nitrate decomposes on heating and gives nitrogen dioxide, a brown gas:
$\mathrm{2Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)}$

questions.question: A student dips an iron nail in copper sulphate solution and a zinc rod in iron sulphate solution. What does she observe in each case after 20 minutes? Write the equations.
answer_steps: Iron nail: a brown coating of copper forms and the blue solution turns pale green. $\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$
Zinc rod: zinc is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron; the pale green solution becomes colourless. $\mathrm{Zn(s) + FeSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + Fe(s)}$
Both are displacement reactions.

questions.question: In the reaction $\mathrm{MnO_{2} + 4HCl \rightarrow MnCl_{2} + 2H_{2}O + Cl_{2}}$, name the substance (i) oxidised (ii) reduced (iii) the oxidising agent.
answer_steps: (i) HCl is oxidised: it loses hydrogen and gives chlorine.
(ii) MnO₂ is reduced: it loses oxygen.
(iii) MnO₂ is the oxidising agent, because it oxidises HCl.

questions.question: Describe an activity to show the electrolysis of water. Which gas collects at each electrode, and in what ratio? Why are a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid added? How will you test the gases?
answer_steps: Fill a plastic mug with water, fix two carbon electrodes through its base and connect them to a 6 V battery. Invert two test tubes filled with water over the electrodes.
Add a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid: pure water conducts electricity very poorly.
Bubbles form at both electrodes: hydrogen at the cathode (negative) and oxygen at the anode (positive).
The volume of hydrogen is double that of oxygen: $\mathrm{2H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow 2H_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)}$
Hydrogen burns with a pop sound near a burning candle; oxygen makes a glowing splinter burst into flame.

questions.question: Give one example each, with a balanced equation, of (i) a combination reaction (ii) a thermal decomposition (iii) a displacement reaction (iv) a precipitation reaction (v) a redox reaction.
answer_steps: (i) $\mathrm{CaO(s) + H_{2}O(l) \rightarrow Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$
(ii) $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)}$
(iii) $\mathrm{Zn(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$
(v) $\mathrm{ZnO + C \rightarrow Zn + CO}$ (ZnO reduced, C oxidised)

questions.question:
Rohan's grandmother keeps her old silver anklets in a cupboard. After a few months they look black. His mother says that the iron gate also needs painting before the monsoon, and that chips must be kept in sealed packets.

(i) What is the black coating on silver called, and what process causes it? (1)

(ii) Why is the iron gate painted before the monsoon? (1)

(iii) What happens to chips kept in an open packet for many days, and how do manufacturers prevent it? OR Name the green coating that forms on copper and explain why it is an example of corrosion. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Silver sulphide; it is corrosion (tarnishing) caused by sulphur compounds in air.
(ii) Paint keeps moisture and air away, so the iron does not rust.

(iii) The oils get oxidised and the chips become rancid (bad smell and taste); packets are flushed with nitrogen and antioxidants are added. OR Basic copper carbonate; copper is slowly attacked by moist carbon dioxide in air, which is corrosion.

questions.question:
In a school laboratory, students mixed solutions in three test tubes:

Test tube A: lead nitrate + potassium iodide

Test tube B: sodium sulphate + barium chloride

Test tube C: copper sulphate + an iron nail

(i) In which test tube does a yellow precipitate form? (1)

(ii) Name the white precipitate formed in test tube B. (1)

(iii) Write the balanced equation for test tube C and state the type of reaction. OR Write the balanced equation for test tube A and state two types of reaction it belongs to. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Test tube A (lead iodide).
(ii) Barium sulphate.

(iii) $\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)}$: displacement reaction. OR $\mathrm{Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(aq) + 2KI(aq) \rightarrow PbI_{2}(s) + 2KNO_{3}(aq)}$: double displacement and precipitation reaction.
